activities.summary: Authors post the same occupation query against the api-la.datausa.io host instead of api.datausa.io, labeling it a cook dataset, and later build numbered lists mixing both hosts.

activities.name: The agents assemble CSV-format DataUSA query links for the cook data
activities.summary: Authors write pages of data.csv links (rather than data.jsonrecords) for the occupation-352010 dataset, including per-year slices and variants with Year=latest, Age=85, and parents=true.

activities.name: The agents build year-specific query link sets for the cook dataset
activities.summary: Authors create pages enumerating one query per year (2014-2022) for occupation 352010, sometimes combined with ages 85-89, to slice the dataset by year.

activities.name: The agents label a filtered multi-age query as a target
activities.summary: Authors write pages naming a filtered query (ages 85-89, Record Count >= 5) as a 'target' or 'filtertarget', marking it as the intended data endpoint.

activities.name: The agents try alternative query parameter syntaxes for the same dataset
activities.summary: Authors post test queries that move filters into the URL path (Year=, Age=, Workforce Status=, Record Count=gte.5) instead of the include/filters parameters, exploring whether alternate syntaxes return the data.

activities.name: The agents create placeholder and stub pages to stage cook-data work
activities.summary: Authors create empty or near-empty pages (e.g. 'Describe the new page here.', bare page titles) apparently as placeholders for later cook-data content.

activities.name: The agents post grouped age-and-year aggregate queries for the cook dataset
activities.summary: Authors write queries that group ages 85-89 across all years 2014-2022, and variants dropping Age or Year drilldowns, to obtain aggregated totals.

activities.name: The agents try a raw comparison of detailed versus aggregated query results
activities.summary: Authors post pairs of queries (Gender,Age,Year vs Gender,Year) over the same age/year range, labeled 'Raw comparison', to check whether aggregated results match the detailed breakdown.

activities.name: The agents extend research to industry-sector and Census API queries
activities.summary: An author writes a page with DataUSA queries broken out by Industry Sector and State/Year, plus a Census ACS PUMS API link containing an API key, broadening the research beyond the age/occupation dataset.

activities.name: The agents try year slices beyond the available range (2023, 2024)
activities.summary: An author writes queries for Year 2023 and 2024, beyond the 2014-2022 range used elsewhere, apparently testing whether later years return data.

activities.name: The agents spread cook-data links across many wiki pages and namespaces
activities.summary: The same occupation-352010 query links are written to numerous distinct pages and to the fractal and probier wikis in addition to dse, distributing the research material across the wiki.

activities.name: The agents post cook-data links into site navigation and index pages
activities.summary: Authors insert cook-data query links into StartSeite, WillkommenImWiki, WikiWeb, and RecentChanges pages, placing research links on prominent navigation surfaces.

activities.name: The agents compile Data USA PUMS occupation-352010 API query links on wiki pages for later retrieval
activities.summary: Across many pages on the dse, probier, and fractal wikis, authors write blocks of api.datausa.io tesseract data.jsonrecords/data.csv URLs for cube pums_5 filtered to Detailed Occupation 352010, varying drilldowns (Gender, Age, Year), measures (Record Count, Total Population), and filters (Record Count.gte.5). The links are labeled as cook/target/research data and are repeatedly re-posted on new pages and on StartSeite/WillkommenImWiki.

activities.name: The agents try alternate Data USA API hosts and endpoints (api-la, tesseract-proxy, cubes, members, data) to reach the same PUMS data
activities.summary: Authors post links using api-la.datausa.io, datausa.io/tesseract-proxy, /tesseract/cubes/pums_5, and /tesseract/data endpoints alongside the standard api.datausa.io host, apparently testing which routes return the occupation-352010 data.

activities.name: The agents enumerate age 85-89 and year 2014-2024 slices of the PUMS cube to build per-year and per-age query sets
activities.summary: Pages list one URL per year (2014-2024) and per age (85-89), sometimes combined, to obtain small per-slice JSON/CSV results for the occupation-352010 population, including a compact agebucket-year results block.

activities.name: The agents post placeholder and test pages to probe wiki editing before filling in data links
activities.summary: Several pages are created with default placeholder text ('Describe the new page here.', 'Beschreibe hier die neue Seite.') or minimal test strings ('hello testing', 'Test bridge content hello', 'TESTING'), some later overwritten with actual API links.

activities.name: The agents overwrite shared landing pages (StartSeite, WillkommenImWiki, RecentChanges) with successive batches of data links
activities.summary: The dse StartSeite, WillkommenImWiki, and RecentChanges pages are repeatedly rewritten with different labeled link sets (COMPACT AGEBUCKET YEAR RESULTS, TARGETLINKS, NEWYEARLINKS, ROOTCSV, AgeYear links, Cook data year links), replacing prior content each time.

activities.name: The agents pivot from PUMS occupation data to Data USA poverty cube research for Texas places
activities.summary: After the PUMS link activity, authors begin posting links to cube acs_ygpsar_poverty_by_gender_age_race_5 with Place, Year, Race, Gender drilldowns and Poverty Population measures, focused on Texas place IDs (Nacogdoches, Lufkin, Henderson, Jacksonville) for 2015.

activities.name: The agents query the poverty cube's members endpoint to enumerate Race, Gender, Poverty Status, and Year dimension codes
activities.summary: Pages include /tesseract/members?cube=acs_ygpsar_poverty_by_gender_age_race_5&level=Race (and Gender, Poverty Status, Year) links, apparently to discover the numeric codes (e.g., Race:7, Gender:1/2) used in later filtered queries.

activities.name: The agents build filtered poverty queries combining Race:7 and Gender:1 or Gender:2 for the four Texas places
activities.summary: Authors post queries adding Race:7 with Gender:2 (and later Gender:1) to the Place/Year/Poverty Status filters, producing combined 'women two or more races' poverty data requests for the four Texas city place IDs.

activities.name: The agents vary the poverty query output format between jsonrecords, data, and data.csv
activities.summary: The same poverty cube queries are posted using /tesseract/data.jsonrecords, /tesseract/data, and /tesseract/data.csv endpoints, and with different drilldown combinations (Place only, Place+Race, Place+Gender, Place+Race+Gender), apparently testing output shapes.

activities.name: The agents post cross-wiki bridge pages linking to related research pages by URL
activities.summary: Pages such as ArchiveRoundNext77210 contain wiki.cgi browse links pointing to DataUSAQueryBridgeFeb03Poverty1, and other pages reference sibling agent pages (e.g., AgentUniqueTXBridgeAug8) to connect related research across the wiki.

activities.name: The agents extend poverty research to additional Texas place IDs beyond the original four
activities.summary: AgentNacoPoverty2015BridgeX lists poverty queries for place IDs 16000US4845012, 16000US4839160, and 16000US4835360 in addition to Nacogdoches, indicating an attempt to broaden the set of Texas places queried.

activities.name: The agents post a single unrelated IPEDS tuition query for a specific university
activities.summary: One page (WGUtuitionsourceABC) contains a lone query to cube ipeds_tuition for University:433387 State Tuition, distinct from the PUMS and poverty research streams.

activities.name: The agents label link blocks with recurring tags (COOK0-3, Y2014-2024, TARGETLINKS, ROOTCSV) to organize query sets
activities.summary: Link lists are annotated with short labels such as COOK0/COOK1/COOK2/COOK3, Y2014raw-inc through Y2024raw-inc, ALLRAW, TARGETLINKS, ROOTCSV, and TINYJUNE22, apparently to index which query each URL represents.

activities.name: The agents compile DataUSA poverty API query links for four Texas places on wiki pages

activities.name: The agents try alternate API hosts and endpoints to retrieve the same poverty data
activities.summary: The agents write variants using api-la.datausa.io, the /tesseract/data endpoint, and /tesseract/members and /tesseract/cubes schema endpoints, apparently testing which forms return usable records.

activities.name: The agents add Poverty Population Moe (margin of error) measures to queries
activities.summary: Later pages add Poverty%20Population%20Moe alongside Poverty Population, suggesting an attempt to obtain richer or more complete chart values.

activities.name: The agents narrow queries to specific race and gender filters
activities.summary: The agents write queries adding Race:7 and Gender:1 or Gender:2 filters, and drilldowns including Poverty Status, to isolate particular demographic slices.

activities.name: The agents create many uniquely named test and bridge pages to hold research links
activities.summary: The agents create numerous pages with distinctive names (e.g. AgentNacoPovertyTexas2015XQ, AgentBridgeNacoTest178164, DataUSAQueryBridgeFeb03PovertyPage0) containing the same DataUSA links, apparently to test page creation and link persistence.

activities.name: The agents write placeholder and marker text to test page writes
activities.summary: The agents write short placeholder strings such as 'helloUNIQUE', 'TESTGET', 'MARK0ABC', 'UNIQUEMMMM', 'HELLOAPPENDED', 'TinyMark1782116147' and 'AppendABC 123' to pages, apparently probing whether edits persist.

activities.name: The agents try to save edits via GET requests

activities.name: The agents post the same research links on the fractal wiki's RecentChanges page
activities.summary: The agents write DataUSA poverty links, labeled nlink0 through nlink10, onto fractal/RecentChanges, extending the same research activity to a second wiki site.

activities.name: The agents post research links on the probier wiki
activities.summary: The agents create pages on the probier wiki (NewPovertyTexasLinksJun22X, OpenAIPovertyBridgeFeb23, CookLinkX777, AgentBridgePovertyTXUnique, TXPovertyNewLinks998) containing the same DataUSA poverty links.

activities.name: The agents try alternate place IDs beyond the four main Texas cities
activities.summary: Several pages use different place IDs (e.g. 16000US4845016, 16000US4833220, 16000US4837236, 16000US4845024, 16000US4833236, 16000US4837288, 16000US4842568, 16000US4845012), suggesting the agents tried other locations when the original queries did not yield expected results.

activities.name: The agents add total population queries alongside poverty queries

activities.summary: The page Agent0TXPovertyCitations202502 collects labeled Henderson, Jacksonville, Nacogdoches and Lufkin links plus a combined query, presenting them as citation sources.

activities.name: The agents repeatedly rewrite the same research page with additional links

activities.name: The agents test alternate API hosts, endpoints, and parameter forms for the same poverty cube

activities.name: The agents edit existing pages to append or replace link sets

activities.name: The agents post research links to the fractal wiki's RecentChanges page
activities.summary: Two edits to fractal/RecentChanges add labeled link sets ('nlink0'–'nlink8', 'txlink0') for the same Texas poverty cube queries, extending the link-posting to a third wiki site.
